what: The answer key for the accuracy suite. Every reference in tree/, and the outcome the engine should produce for it.
authored: Each expected answer was written down before the engine ran. Positions are stamped by tools/stamp-positions.mjs; the answers are not.
neverAScore: This key produces a matrix, one row per shape. It has no total, no percentage and no overall row, and it must stay impossible to turn into one.

expectSemantics._: Seven outcomes, matching the engine's Resolution union. `expect` is the outcome a correct engine should produce, not what today's engine does: a .vue reference expects to be found, which is what lets the matrix say "0 of 8, no reader" out loud. Where today's engine is known to differ, `knownGap` says so.
expectSemantics.resolved: Points at exactly one asset, and `target` names it.
expectSemantics.resolved-pattern: One reference standing for N assets; `target` is the full list.
expectSemantics.dynamic: The path is assembled at runtime. There is no static path to resolve, and nobody typed a wrong one.
expectSemantics.out-of-scope: An absolute URL, a protocol-relative URL, an npm package specifier, or a real file the engine deliberately does not index. Like `discarded`, this covers two engine behaviours, and the measuring harness must accept either: the engine may emit a reference whose resolution is `out-of-scope` (a real .mp4 it can see but will not index), or emit nothing at all (an absolute URL, dropped by isExternalUrl before it ever becomes a reference; a link@href the predicate refuses). It must not accept a resolved, broken or rewritten outcome.
expectSemantics.unresolved-alias: Alias-shaped, with no rule that maps it.
expectSemantics.broken: A well-formed, asserted reference to a file that does not exist. A finding.
expectSemantics.discarded: Must not be treated as a live reference. The word covers two engine behaviours, and both satisfy it: the engine may emit nothing at all (a url() inside a comment is never collected), or emit a reference whose resolution is `discarded`. The measuring harness accepts either. It must not accept a resolved, broken or rewritten outcome.
expectSemantics.UNDECIDED: Nobody has decided which outcome is correct. `candidates` lists the possibilities. These do not fail the integrity check; they fail the measuring suite, which runs --strict, and they are questions for a person rather than measurements.

servingRoots.why: Serving root #1. A conventional app with a public directory.

Serving root #2. A repository can have many public directories, not one. brand.png, logo.png, img/hero.jpg and the three theme-*.png files exist in both apps and are different pictures, so a reference resolving against the wrong root is visible rather than coincidentally right.

The site's own directory is the serving root, so every file beside index.html is web-reachable, templates and partials included. The public-dir caveat applies to everything rather than to one subtree.
A fourth root, in an app whose source is entirely in file types nothing reads.

A VitePress site's served folder: docs/public/, served from the root, beside a config directory (docs/.vitepress/) rather than a config file, with the site's package.json two levels up, not beside it.

notServingRoots.why: A directory named `public` that serves nothing: it holds illustrations for a guide about a project that has a serving root. None of the five validation repositories has one, so nothing else tests this risk. It is not a serving root. Detection by name alone would claim it; detection also requires a project file beside a `public/`, and docs-examples/ holds none, so it is rejected.

aliases._: From tree/tsconfig.json, and in sites/kit-app and sites/nuxt-app from their tsconfig.json, which extends the config the framework generates (.svelte-kit/, .nuxt/). apps/web and sites/vue-app also map @ in their Vite configs. Anything else that is alias-shaped maps nowhere on purpose. tree/tsconfig.json also sets baseUrl to the tree root, where a bare import that no key maps is looked for before any package.

imageSizesNote: The tree holds no image that WebP makes larger, because real photographs do not have that property: 4 sources at 14 sizes down to 8x8, 56 combinations, all came out smaller as WebP, lossless and lossy alike. The property belongs to synthetic placeholders, and fixtures/partial-pattern covers it as a conversion fixture. This tree measures reference detection. Every asset still records its real byte size and hash, so probe and encode coverage can be added later without rebuilding the tree.

shapes.label: img@src
shapes.motivation: The position everything else is compared against.

shapes.label: markup swallowed by an unclosed raw-text element
shapes.motivation: In markdown an unclosed raw-text tag mid-sentence is masked, because CommonMark requires a raw-text block to begin a line. In a .html file there is no prose: an unclosed <style> opens a raw-text element, and a browser renders nothing after it either. These four exist to read zero; a non-zero count means the engine disagrees with the browser about what the page shows.

shapes.label: img@srcset, one candidate
shapes.motivation: A srcset with no descriptor list at all, which parses differently from a list of one.

shapes.label: img@srcset, x descriptors
shapes.motivation: A srcset row must distinguish 8 of 9 from 9 of 9.

shapes.label: img@srcset, w descriptors
shapes.motivation: The same shape with width descriptors and a sizes attribute beside it.

shapes.label: source@srcset
shapes.motivation: picture/source, where the candidate list is the only content.

shapes.label: source@src
shapes.motivation: Inside video and audio, where source carries src rather than srcset.

shapes.label: video@src
shapes.motivation: Points at a real file the engine does not index: the out-of-scope case that is not a URL.

shapes.label: video@poster
shapes.motivation: An image position on a non-image element, beside video@src so the two cannot be confused.

shapes.label: audio@src
shapes.motivation: As video@src, in an element that is easy to forget.

shapes.label: embed@src
shapes.motivation: Carries both a PDF and an image, so the outcome depends on the target rather than the tag.

shapes.label: input@src
shapes.motivation: type="image" is the only input that takes a src, and it is routinely missed.

shapes.label: track@src
shapes.motivation: A caption file: a real file, never an asset.

shapes.label: link@href asserted as an icon
shapes.motivation: The icon branch of `linkImageClaim`: any rel token containing "icon", which covers icon, shortcut icon, apple-touch-icon and mask-icon.

shapes.label: link@href asserted as a preloaded image
shapes.motivation: The preload branch of `linkImageClaim`, rel=preload with as=image: a separate return from the icon branch, so it fails separately.
shapes.singleReason: One instance, not padded. Two more rel=preload links added only so the row reads three would shape the tree by what makes a row readable rather than by what real pages contain. Real pages will supply more: rel=preload as=image is how a modern page preloads its LCP hero, so like `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` it is not exotic, just untested.

shapes.label: link@href the predicate refuses
shapes.motivation: A stylesheet link and a manifest link sit in the same attribute as an icon and must not be treated alike. This row is what `linkImageClaim` refuses, so it is homogeneous and a zero is the correct reading; a non-zero count would be the failure.

shapes.label: meta@content naming a link-preview image
shapes.motivation: A page names the picture its link preview shows in a meta tag (og:image, twitter:image, msapplication-TileImage), and often nowhere else, so an engine that skips the tag reports a used image dead. The meta tag's property or name is the claim. Linked and never rewritten: the sites that fetch previews read the file named here, and may not decode a converted format.

shapes.label: a@href naming an image
shapes.motivation: A link that hands over an image file: a download link, or a caption that opens the full picture. The value's extension is the claim, so a link to a page or a PDF stays out. Linked and never rewritten: a person following the link expects the format it names.

shapes.label: object@data
shapes.motivation: An object element is an asset position in real documents: object@data is the same position as embed@src, in a different element.

shapes.label: iframe@src
shapes.motivation: A path-shaped attribute that must never become a finding: precision, not recall.

shapes.label: SVG image@href
shapes.motivation: The modern spelling.

shapes.label: SVG image@xlink:href
shapes.motivation: The legacy spelling, which is still most of what is in the wild.

shapes.label: SVG feImage
shapes.motivation: A filter primitive that loads an image, in both spellings.

shapes.label: a path in an HTML attribute Upfly does not read
shapes.motivation: A path naming an image where Upfly reads none: a tooltip, a custom attribute, or data-src and imagesrcset, which a lazy-loading script or the browser may load and Upfly does not read. Declined and counted, so the report shows what was skipped; the row reads backwards: an outcome other than discarded is the failure.

shapes.label: <style> element carrying CSS
shapes.motivation: CSS reached through HTML, which is a different path into the CSS parser.

shapes.label: style="" attribute carrying CSS
shapes.motivation: The same again, one element at a time.

shapes.label: a path spelled with HTML character references
shapes.motivation: /gallery/a&b.png is 20 source characters and 16 decoded, and getting that wrong corrupts a file on rewrite. A character reference is how the path is spelled, so it takes precedence over the construct the path sits in, exactly as an absolute URL does.

shapes.label: a percent-encoded path
shapes.motivation: Two references that look alike and resolve oppositely: one decodes to a file that exists, the other is the name of a file that exists as written.

shapes.label: url() unquoted
shapes.motivation: Three spellings of one thing; a parser that handles two is a parser that fails on the third.

shapes.label: url() single-quoted
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: url() double-quoted
shapes.motivation: As above, and the only spelling that can carry a filename with spaces.

shapes.label: url() inside another function
shapes.motivation: cross-fade and var()'s fallback: the walker has to recurse to reach the url. A url that is merely not the whole value, as after a gradient, is not what this shape names, and image-set has its own row.

shapes.label: image-set()
shapes.motivation: Standard spelling, with and without url().

shapes.label: -webkit-image-set()
shapes.motivation: The prefixed spelling, which is still what ships.

shapes.label: url() inside a comment
shapes.motivation: Must be discarded. Rewriting one edits a file for no reason.

shapes.label: url() inside a selector
shapes.motivation: Must be discarded. An attribute selector whose value contains url(...) is text, not a reference.

shapes.label: url() behind a custom property
shapes.motivation: The declaration holds the url; the use site holds a var().

shapes.label: @font-face src
shapes.motivation: A real file the engine does not index, reached through CSS rather than HTML.

shapes.label: url(#fragment)
shapes.motivation: A same-document reference. Never a path.

shapes.label: url() in .scss
shapes.motivation: The CSS adapter has to cover all three extensions, not only `.css`.

shapes.label: url($variable)
shapes.motivation: Not knowable until the preprocessor runs. Nobody typed a wrong path.

shapes.label: url() with trailing #{} interpolation
shapes.motivation: The partial-pattern shape: one reference standing for three files that all exist.

shapes.label: url() with leading #{} interpolation
shapes.motivation: Harder than a trailing one: the prefix that would anchor a glob is the unknown part.

shapes.label: url() in .less
shapes.motivation: The third dialect.

shapes.label: url(@variable)
shapes.motivation: As scss.variable, in Less syntax.

shapes.label: url() with @{} interpolation
shapes.motivation: As scss.interpolation, in Less syntax.

shapes.label: static ESM import of an image
shapes.motivation: The reference the bundler resolves, so breaking one breaks the build.

shapes.label: a type-only import or re-export naming an image
shapes.motivation: `import type` and `export type ... from` are erased when TypeScript compiles, so no file is loaded. Taken by the guessing rule, the path would be linked and a rewrite would change a module name only the type checker reads; declined, it is counted and never linked, so the row reads backwards: an outcome other than discarded is the failure.

shapes.label: import through a tsconfig paths alias
shapes.motivation: Turns the unresolved-alias bucket into real links.

shapes.label: import through an alias that maps nowhere
shapes.motivation: Its own bucket. Not broken, not dynamic, but unmapped.

shapes.label: a bare package specifier
shapes.motivation: A bare specifier in module syntax is read as module resolution reads it: through the tsconfig's baseUrl and paths, then as a package, and never beside the importing file. A file inside a package is out-of-scope rather than unresolved-alias: the file exists, it is just not ours. A name nothing finds is broken. The row holds imports, a require() and a plain string constant, so it is named for what the path is rather than for `import`.

shapes.label: require() of an image
shapes.motivation: A repository built over ten years has both module systems.

shapes.label: new URL('./x.png', import.meta.url)
shapes.motivation: The asset pattern Vite and webpack 5 document. Its first argument is a URL, resolved against the module's own URL, so a bare name is a file beside the module. Vite reads the name before the browser does: through its aliases, then beside the module, then as a package. A name an alias maps and misses is unresolved-alias, one a package holds out-of-scope, and one found nowhere else broken.

shapes.label: import.meta.glob('./img/*.png')
shapes.motivation: Vite's glob import loads every file its patterns match: one string or an array of them, a `!` pattern leaving files out, `**` crossing folders and braces offering alternatives. Read as a plain string, `./img/*.png` names no file, and every image it loads would be reported unused. Four instances: a string, `**`, braces through an alias, and an array with a negation.

shapes.label: require.context('./img', true, /\.png$/)
shapes.motivation: webpack's context bundles every file under a folder whose path from it, written from `./`, a regular expression matches: that folder alone or every folder below it, as the second argument says. Read as a plain string, the folder names no file, and every image it bundles would be reported unused. Four instances: one folder only, the folder alone with webpack's defaults, an expression that leaves some images out, and an expression only the build can work out.

shapes.label: import.meta.webpackContext('./img', { regExp: /\.png$/ })
shapes.motivation: webpack's `import.meta.webpackContext`, the ES module form of `require.context`, bundles every file under a folder whose path from it, written from `./`, the `regExp` option matches: that folder alone or every folder below it, as the `recursive` option says. Its other options change how the files load, not which. Read as a plain string, the folder names no file, and every image it bundles would be reported unused. Four instances: one folder only, options that change only how the files load, an expression that leaves some images out, and an expression only the build can work out.

shapes.label: template literal, one unknown segment
shapes.motivation: partial-pattern. Standing for N files that all exist.

shapes.label: a pattern matching only some of the files it names
shapes.motivation: A pattern row that only ever saw three-of-three would not notice a two-of-three. No adapter can name this row: the distinction is which of the files the pattern names actually exist, which only the resolver can see, so the adapters emit js.template.pattern or scss.interpolation.trailing and the key draws the line.

shapes.label: template literal, nothing static left
shapes.motivation: A base and a name, both variables. Not knowable.

shapes.label: path assembled by concatenation
shapes.motivation: The same thing without a template literal, which is easy to miss.

shapes.label: path assembled by concatenation, one unknown segment
shapes.motivation: A + chain in which no literal is itself a complete path is read exactly as its template twin is, so a fixed directory and one unknown in the name is a pattern here too. Four instances, deliberately varied: through a literal prefix (paths.ts:40), through a same-file const (paths.ts:26), inside a JSX attribute (IconBadge.tsx), and through a declared alias (crests.ts).

shapes.label: a path-shaped string literal
shapes.motivation: A guess, not an assertion: an unresolved one is dropped rather than reported.

shapes.label: a literal path in a JSX attribute
shapes.motivation: Asserted, unlike a bare string, because the attribute says what it is.

shapes.label: a JSX meta@content naming a link-preview image
shapes.motivation: The same meta tag, written by a layout component. The JSX reader takes the position from the list the HTML adapter reads, so it can break without the HTML row, and the other way round.

shapes.label: a JSX a@href naming an image
shapes.motivation: The same link, written in a component. Its own row for the reason the meta tag has one: the JSX reader is a second reader of the shared list.

shapes.label: a JSX link@href asserted as an icon
shapes.motivation: The icon link of `html.link.href.icon`, written by a layout component. Its own row because the JSX shape follows the claim: an icon keeps its format and a preloaded image does not, so the JSX reader can give a component's icon the preload's shape without the HTML row noticing.

shapes.label: a path in a JSX attribute read as text
shapes.motivation: A path written where an attribute is display text or a component's own prop. The JSX reader declines it however it is spelled, and a declined value must never become a link, so the row reads backwards: an outcome other than discarded is the failure.

shapes.label: CSS-in-JS carrying a url()
shapes.motivation: CSS the CSS adapter never sees, because it is inside a template literal.

shapes.label: ![alt](path)
shapes.motivation: The ordinary markdown image.

shapes.label: [text](path)
shapes.motivation: A plain link to an image, which hands over the file itself: linked, and never rewritten.

shapes.label: ![alt][label]
shapes.motivation: The path is not at the use site; it is in a definition further down.
shapes.absent: Three are present in the tree and none can be keyed, because the use site carries no path at all: `![The screenshot][shot]` names a label. The paths live in the definitions at the foot of the file and are keyed as md.reference-definition. A row here would count label lookups, not references. Deliberately empty; the coverage it stands for is md.reference-definition's.

shapes.label: [label]: path
shapes.motivation: Where a reference-style link actually keeps its path.

shapes.label: [label]: path, used by a link
shapes.motivation: A definition a plain link uses hands over the file itself, as the link does: linked, and never rewritten.

shapes.label: raw HTML inside markdown
shapes.motivation: Markdown hands it through untouched, so it is still HTML and still a reference.

shapes.label: a style attribute inside markdown
shapes.motivation: CSS inside HTML inside markdown, three parsers deep.

shapes.label: a path named in prose
shapes.motivation: Reported, never rewritten. Rewriting prose corrupts a sentence.

shapes.label: a path inside a fenced code block
shapes.motivation: An example, not a reference.

shapes.label: a path inside an indented code block
shapes.motivation: The older fence syntax, which a fence-aware masker can still miss.

shapes.label: a path inside inline code
shapes.motivation: Backticks mid-sentence, which is neither prose nor a fence.

shapes.label: an image path in YAML frontmatter
shapes.motivation: No adapter reads frontmatter yet, so these record a known gap rather than a success. Measured scope: 4 instances across the real corpus, all in eleventy-docs.

shapes.label: an image path nested inside frontmatter
shapes.motivation: The same gap, nested. A different key at a different depth is what makes it a class rather than three files.

shapes.label: an ESM import in MDX
shapes.motivation: MDX is markdown that can import.

shapes.label: a JSX attribute in MDX
shapes.motivation: And markdown that can hold JSX.

shapes.label: a webmanifest icon entry
shapes.motivation: Asserted by the manifest schema, unlike an arbitrary JSON string.

shapes.label: a webmanifest screenshot or shortcut icon
shapes.motivation: The same file, two more keys, both routinely missed.

shapes.label: an image path in an ordinary JSON config
shapes.motivation: A guess. Every package.json in the world would otherwise produce findings.

shapes.label: a glob in a JSON config
shapes.motivation: `**/*.png` is not a path, and must not become one.

shapes.label: an ESM import in the frontmatter fence
shapes.motivation: The fence is JavaScript; the body is not.

shapes.label: a literal path in the template body
shapes.motivation: The body is HTML, and the adapter has to switch.

shapes.label: a path from an expression in the template body
shapes.motivation: Declared in the fence, used in the body.
shapes.absent: Present in the tree and keyed under a different row. `` carries no path: the path is the string constant in the fence, which is keyed as js.string.literal. Counting the use site as well would double-count one reference, which the matrix must not do.

shapes.label: an extension inside a regular expression
shapes.motivation: Source code about images is not a reference to one.
shapes.absent: Present in the tree at apps/web/src/lib/decoys.ts (`/\.(png|jpe?g|svg)$/i`) and invisible to the text scan, because a regex escapes the dot: the bytes read `\.(png`, and `.png` never occurs. So the checker cannot demand a key entry for it, and none is given. This row measures nothing, and an engine that did extract a path from a regex would not be caught here.

shapes.label: a <style> element in an .astro file
shapes.motivation: Scoped CSS, reached through a third parser.

shapes.label: a reference inside .vue
shapes.motivation: A reference in a file type nothing reads can break while every instrument reports success.

shapes.label: a reference inside .svelte
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: a reference inside .njk
shapes.motivation: As above. eleventy-docs is full of these.

shapes.label: a reference inside .liquid
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: a reference inside .erb
shapes.motivation: As above. railsgirls-com is an ERB site.

shapes.label: a reference inside .php
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: a filename inside a code comment
shapes.motivation: Precision has no meaning without these: a tree of only real references cannot produce a false positive.

shapes.label: a path inside a log message
shapes.motivation: Indistinguishable from a reference by syntax alone, and it points at nothing.

shapes.label: a name one character from a real file
shapes.motivation: The difference between a broken reference and a string that was never one.

shapes.label: extension-shaped text that is not a path
shapes.motivation: A media type, a class name, a flag, a name with an extra extension.

shapes.label: a glob rather than a path
shapes.motivation: Matches files without naming one.

shapes.label: a backslash-separated path
shapes.motivation: Nothing in this tree is addressed this way.

shapes.label: a real file with a query string or fragment
shapes.motivation: Not a decoy in the end: these resolve. Kept in the row because they look like one and are the case an over-eager stripper gets wrong in the other direction.

shapes.label: a data: URI
shapes.motivation: Never a path. Rewriting one is a corruption.

shapes.label: an absolute URL
shapes.motivation: Out-of-scope: real, reachable, not ours.

shapes.label: a protocol-relative URL
shapes.motivation: Starts with // and is not a path, which is exactly what it looks like.
